content:
Straight Lines is where JEE quietly tests speed with slope, distance and intercept forms. Most droppers I coach leak marks on the angle between two lines and the foot of the perpendicular. Take the free JEE Straight Lines online test below. It holds 15 exam-pattern MCQs with instant scoring and worked answers. Target 12 out of 15.

What JEE asks from Straight Lines

  • Slope, inclination and the intercept forms of a line.
  • Angle between two lines and the perpendicular condition.
  • Distance of a point from a line and between parallels.
  • Foot of perpendicular, image and reflection problems.
  • Centroid, orthocentre and circumcentre of a triangle.

Formulas and facts to revise first

  • Parallel lines share a slope, so their coefficients stay proportional.
  • Two lines meet at right angles when the slope product equals minus one.
  • The point to line distance divides the line value by root a squared plus b squared.
  • The centroid simply averages the three vertex coordinates.
  • A right triangle puts its circumcentre at the hypotenuse midpoint.

Mistakes that cost JEE marks

  • Forgetting the modulus in the point to line distance formula.
  • Swapping a slope for its negative reciprocal at the wrong step.
  • Confusing the orthocentre with the circumcentre in a right triangle.
  • Reading intercepts off the wrong axis under time pressure.

quiz.title: JEE Straight Lines Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen exam-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: A line has a positive slope and a negative y-intercept. Which quadrants does it pass through?
questions.explanation: It rises left to right and cuts the y-axis below the origin. So it crosses quadrants I, III and IV.

questions.q: A line passes through (2, 2) and its axis intercepts sum to 9. One such line is:
questions.explanation: With intercepts a and 9 − a, the point gives a = 3 or 6. The choice a = 3 yields 2x + y = 6.

questions.q: The lines y = mx + c and y = mx + d with c ≠ d have how many solutions?
questions.explanation: Equal slopes with different intercepts stay parallel. Parallel lines never meet, so there are zero solutions.

questions.q: Which triangle do the lines x + y = 0, 3x + y − 4 = 0 and x + 3y − 4 = 0 form?
questions.explanation: Two of the angles share the same tangent value. So the triangle is isosceles.

questions.q: A ray through (1, 2) reflects off the x-axis and then passes through (5, 3). Find the x-coordinate of the reflection point.
questions.explanation: Reflect (1, 2) to (1, −2), then join it to (5, 3). Setting y = 0 gives x = 13/5.

questions.q: Find the distance between the parallel lines x + y = 1 and x + y = 5.
questions.explanation: Distance = |5 − 1| divided by the root of 1 plus 1. That equals 4/√2.

questions.q: The line 3x − √3y + 2 = 0 makes what angle with the x-axis?
questions.explanation: The slope works out to √3, whose inclination is 60°.

questions.q: Find the line through (2, −1) perpendicular to y = 4x + 3.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular slope is −1/4. The point-slope form then gives x + 4y + 2 = 0.
Rewrite the first as 6x + 8y − 18 = 0. The gap is 3 over the root of 100, which is 3/10.

questions.q: Find the acute angle between y − √3x − 5 = 0 and √3y − x + 6 = 0.
questions.explanation: The slopes are √3 and 1/√3. The angle formula then gives 30°.

questions.q: Find the foot of the perpendicular from the origin to x + y − 4 = 0.
questions.explanation: The perpendicular through the origin is y = x. It meets the line at (2, 2).

questions.q: When are a1x + b1y + c1 = 0 and a2x + b2y + c2 = 0 parallel?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines share a slope, so a1/a2 = b1/b2. Distinct lines keep the c ratio different.

questions.q: Find the orthocentre of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3).
questions.explanation: The right angle sits at the origin. In a right triangle the orthocentre is that vertex.

questions.q: Find the centroid of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3).
questions.explanation: Average the coordinates directly. The centroid is (4/3, 1).

questions.q: Find the circumcentre of the right triangle with vertices (0, 0), (4, 0) and (0, 3).
questions.explanation: The circumcentre of a right triangle is the hypotenuse midpoint. That midpoint is (2, 3/2).
